subject: Verdane pilot: acceptance criteria, KPI owners, and cost-splitting plan
content:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Malhotra <aisha@verdane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Verdane pilot: acceptance criteria, KPI owners, and cost-splitting plan

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Thanks again for a great kickoff earlier today. Per our call, I wanted to capture a short post-call recap with concrete acceptance criteria, owners, and a suggested cost split for the 4-week pilot so we can get alignment and lock dates. I attached a one-page success metrics workbook and a small sample payload set for validation.

Proposed pilot scope (high level)
- Workload: customer chat summarization + priority classification for 100k daily messages (30-token average reply).
- Duration: 4 weeks of active testing after sandbox ingest (estimated start: Nov 22).
- Success window: operational stability + quality thresholds for the primary intents.

Acceptance criteria (minimum to pass)
1) Latency: median generation latency <= 180ms for tail trimmed requests (95th <= 350ms) on the agreed test harness.
2) Throughput: sustained ≥ 60 requests/sec at 300 token bursts using the sample load.
3) Cost: amortized cost/token <= $0.0009 (including caching and batching effects) while meeting latency targets.
4) Quality: intent classification accuracy >= 92% and summarization ROUGE-L >= 0.62 on the supplied eval prompts.

Owners / roles
- Redwood runtime & ops: Ben Carter — responsible for perf tuning, batching, and quantization recommendations.
- Program manager: Marissa Cole — runbook, telemetry dashboard, and weekly cadence.
- Verdane PO: Aisha Malhotra — dataset validation, acceptance tests, and sign-off.

Suggested cost-splitting (pilot economics)
- Redwood covers baseline infra for sandbox + 50% of peak test hours for the first 2 weeks to accelerate tuning.
- Verdane covers token/throughput costs for production-like runs and any incremental storage beyond the provided sample set.
- We will capture actual run-hours and token usage daily and reconcile at the end of week 2 and week 4.

Next steps / asks
1) Aisha: confirm you can provide the final test set (expanded from the sample payloads) by Nov 15.
2) Ben: can you confirm the initial perf runbook and target test harness by EOD Nov 10?
3) Marissa: I suggest a weekly 30-min sync (Mon 9am PT) + a mid-pilot ops review on Dec 13.

Attachments: Verdane_POC_success_metrics_v1.xlsx (workbook), verdane_sample_payloads.jsonl (1000 example records)

Appreciate the quick confirmation so we can finalize a Statement of Work and the HubSpot timeline.

—
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Aisha Malhotra <aisha@verdane.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Russo <tom.russo@verdane.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Verdane pilot: acceptance criteria, KPI owners, and cost-splitting plan

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 100k/day figure is a peak estimate; our initial seed dataset for the pilot is closer to 15k/day, but we want to validate spikes to 100k.
- For quality, we can own the human-reviewed ground-truth for intent labels; we will need Redwood to own summarization evals (ROUGE + human spot-check).
- On cost-splitting: Verdane can take the incremental token hours for production-like runs but would ask Redwood to cap the first 40 dev hours used for kernel experimentation.

We can deliver the final test set by Nov 14 (end of day) — that should give you a week for sandbox ingest before the proposed Nov 22 start.

I also attached a short security checklist we need for our procurement team (SOC2 evidence and data retention policy).

Best,
Aisha
VP Product, Verdane AI

On Fri, Nov 6, 2026 at 2:22 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai> wrote:

>
> Based on Aisha's note, Ben and I pared down the acceptance criteria to two tiers:
> - Minimum (must pass): latency, throughput, and intent accuracy as listed above.
> - Stretch (nice-to-have): median latency <= 140ms, cost/token <= $0.0007, summarization ROUGE-L >= 0.68.
>
> Ben, I nudged the ops runbook to mark two engineering spikes for kernel tuning (Nov 23–24) and batch configuration (Nov 29). Can you confirm the rough ETA for perf numbers after the first tuning spike?
>
> Also looping in Marissa to lock the weekly check-ins and the pilot acceptance gate checklist. I captured a small line item for the DocuSign SOW; we'll draft that once we have firm dates.
>
> Thanks,
> Karthik
>
